intro.text: One of the Silver Kingdoms of Roshar in the Heraldic Epochs. Like the others, its name is symmetrical, following Vorin tradition.

description.text: Valhav stretched across middle and eastern Roshar, from the Purelake in the west to Alethela in the east. It bordered Rishir to the north, Makabakam to the south and southwest, Sela Tales to the west and the Tarat Sea to the south, close to islands held by Rishir and Thalath.
Valhav's people wrote in the Dawnchant, at first simply using it to spell out their own language, then adapting it into a script of their own.
It took in the Horneater Peaks and a small part of the Purelake. Several great rivers crossed it, most running north or south into the Reshi or Tarat seas.

items.text: Valhav's peoples varied. Most were pale with violet eyes, but many, above all in the south, looked like their neighbours in Alethela, tan with dark hair, and some were darker still. The men of the Horneater Peaks were pale too, but tall and often red-haired.
Valhav's people wrote in the Dawnchant, at first simply using it to spell out their own language, then adapting it into a script of their own.
Singers lived in the land before humans came to Roshar from Ashyn.

The humans were first given the land that became Shin Kak Nish. Within a generation they invaded the singers' lands, killing many and driving them out, a history forgotten until the Eila Stele was found.
In the millennia after Aharietiam, Valhav collapsed. Its old lands are now split among several kingdoms, the largest share governed by Jah Keved.

told.title: A land of singers
told.text: Singers lived in the land that became Valhav before humans came to Roshar.

told.title: Taken from the singers
told.text: Singers lived in the land that became Valhav until humans, given a home in what became Shin Kak Nish, turned on them, killing or driving out the singers and taking their lands. The tale was lost until the Eila Stele was found.

told.title: Valhav is founded
told.text: Valhav was founded in the age of the Silver Kingdoms. Each Desolation threw its people back, sometimes as far as stone tools, and each time the returning Heralds, Kalak among them, helped them rise again.

told.title: Desolation after Desolation
told.text: Desolations struck Valhav again and again, along with the rest of Roshar.

told.title: The Last Desolation
told.text: About 4,500 years ago, the Last Desolation struck a world still weak from the Desolation before it. Weary of their torment, nine of the Heralds then refused to go back, leaving Taln to bear it alone.

told.title: The Desolations end
told.text: With no more Desolations to ravage it, Valhav could advance further than ever before.

told.title: Valhav falls apart
told.text: At some point after the Last Desolation, Valhav collapsed. Its old lands are now split among several kingdoms, the largest share ruled by Jah Keved.
